issue.title: Re-measure the SASE_TEST_SELECTION_DEPTH table before recommending depth 3
issue.description: The static-selection implementation reproduces the epic plan's median-selection-rate table at depths 0-2, but its depth-3 median measures 9.9%, not the plan's assumed 5.5% -- depth 3 is ~2.4x more expensive than the plan believes. The epic plan's own remediation advice for a nonzero false-negative rate is to raise SASE_TEST_SELECTION_DEPTH to 3, so that advice should not be followed without re-measuring against real usage first. Proposed by epic sase-fp's land phase (sase-fp.8.3), originally measured during sase-fp.1 (Static import-graph selection engine).

evidence.note: Epic sase-g3 re-measured depth 3 against real history and the cost is now bounded with evidence, which changes what this bead needs to decide. 'just selection-backtest --limit 150 --include-descendant-baseline --baseline 96183d71b' at 4651ed199 over 63 commits with usable ground truth: moving the closure-only arm from depth 2 to depth 3 lifts mean recall 96.0% -> 99.2%, p10 85.3% -> 100%, worst 23.5% -> 81.3%, cuts blind-spot commits 13 -> 5 and missed test files 116 -> 11 (91% of the measured blind spot recovered). The cost side reproduces this bead's finding rather than the plan's assumption: median selection 6.4% -> 8.8% of the suite, p90 11.9% -> 21.2%, and on src/sase/agent_lanes.py specifically 110 -> 255 files / 1,117 -> 2,514 tests / 57s -> 164s serial on athena. Replayed escalation rate rises 23/63 -> 28/63, though those are whole-commit historical diffs and therefore an upper bound on what a working-tree change selects. sase-g3 shipped depth+1 only when the coverage-contexts baseline is missing or stale (the named rule no-baseline-depth-boost), so the unconditional depth-3 question this bead owns is still open -- but it can now be decided on measured recall-for-cost rather than on the plan's 5.5% figure. Proposed by sase-g3.5, corroborated at land time by sase-g3.land.

payload.entry: Backlog triage 2026-08-06 (master 25285417d), closed as one group. The owner asked for the seven highest-impact open tasks and for everything else to be closed with a reason; these nine are the epic sase-fp aftermath that improves an already-working lane rather than fixing broken behavior. Specifically: sase-ft (share the import-graph cache host-locally, ~8.4s once per fresh workspace), sase-fu (re-measure the depth-3 selection table — advisory only, the default is still depth 2), sase-fv (correlate CI failures with local selection manifests), sase-fw (attribute the escalation-rate delta to coverage contexts), sase-fx (coverage-contexts baseline beyond 14-day retention — degradation is graceful, it falls back to the static closure), sase-fz (lazy Pillow import to drop _setup-visual from two lanes), sase-g0 (32s whole-repo collect-only in the contract-manifest test, which now costs the full lane rather than the default scoped one), sase-g1 (a single 'gw22' xdist worker-crash node ID polluting the selection-health store — deletable by hand today), and sase-fg (88s of archive-scale dismissed-bundle setup, which the scoped lane only pays when selected). The one member of this class kept open is sase-g9, because a thin coverage baseline winning on mtime degrades selection ground truth and can therefore make a scoped check pass when it should fail — a correctness problem, not a cost one. Refile any of these individually with fresh measurements if the two-speed lane's cost or accuracy becomes an actual blocker.

payload.close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-06: test-selection / test-lane cost, caching, measurement, retention, or metric-hygiene follow-up from epic sase-fp — not a correctness defect. Cut to bring the ready task queue from 30 to 7.
